i.norm: Verifies cross-encoding behaviour: encoding an ASCII string as UTF-16LE bytes, then reinterpreting those raw bytes as UTF-8 produces a string where every original character is followed by a null byte (U+0000). UTF-16LE stores each ASCII character as two bytes: the character byte followed by 0x00. When these bytes are passed to a UTF-8 decoder, each ASCII byte decodes as itself, while each 0x00 byte decodes as the null character U+0000.
Encode using UTF-16LE: each ASCII character becomes (char_byte, 0x00)
Reinterpret the UTF-16LE byte sequence as UTF-8. The 0x00 padding bytes from UTF-16LE survive as U+0000 null characters.

UTF-16LE turns "[NQ.38g~9u=YGOxnW" (18 chars) into 36 bytes. Each original character survives, interleaved with a null character ('\0'). Build the expected value with explicit null chars to make the pattern clear.
